scope: Proposition 2.3 (Construction at every scale) of the manuscript “Quantitative lower bounds for trace reconstruction” (preprints/quantitative-lower-bounds-for-trace-reconstruction-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 122 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 6b28f84fe939dfe5), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 7. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix B, ζ, c+ and the parameters of this section. Along every sequence with n → ∞ and δ3 log n → ∞, for all sufficiently large instances there exist level-i pairs satisfying Definition 2.2 simultaneously for 0 ≤ i ≤ D. The choices of C, ω depend only on δ and obey the displayed logarithmic bounds, and one MB depending only on B works at every level.
